purpose: Qualify the structural decomposition of the known deterministic at-least-draw response policy after 1.C1 ...d1 using only Connect Four rules and that policy, without any perfect-play terminal-line classification.
race_lemmas: If P0 owns D3 under the policy, P1 already owns D2. If P0 also owns E3,F3,G3, the above-response policy has already given P1 E2,F2,G2. Therefore a purported P0 D3-G3 completion is preempted by the earlier P1 D2-G2 completion.

If P0 owns D5 under the policy, P1 already owns D4. If P0 also owns E5,F5,G5, the above-response policy has already given P1 E4,F4,G4. Therefore a purported P0 D5-G5 completion is preempted by the earlier P1 D4-G4 completion.
interpretation: The deterministic policy is total on every qualified nonterminal policy state and permits no P0 terminal win.
Static blocker coverage alone accounts for 67 of 69 geometric lines.
Exactly two remaining line obligations require temporal first-win/race reasoning rather than static ownership blockers.
This supplies a concrete witness that race-generated blockers/preemption are the missing ingredient beyond ordinary WSL subset coverage in this policy family.
non_claims: This is not a perfect-play terminal-line classification.
This does not prove that the same compact certificate family is complete for the standard center-opening P0 win.
The exhaustive policy-state traversal is qualification evidence for the compact certificate, not the desired production proof mechanism.
